question: A caller says they are calling from SBI Bank and your ATM card is blocked. They ask for the 6-digit OTP just sent to your phone to unblock it. What should you do?
options: Share the OTP immediately so card is not permanently blocked
Cut the call immediately and never share the OTP
Ask them to confirm your name first, then share
explanation: Banks NEVER ask for OTP over the phone. Legitimate bank SMS explicitly states 'DO NOT SHARE WITH ANYONE'.

question: A buyer on OLX agrees to buy your old bicycle for ₹3,000. He sends a UPI QR code and says 'Scan this and enter your UPI PIN to receive ₹3,000 in your account'. What will happen?
options: You will receive ₹3,000 instantly in your bank account
₹3,000 will be deducted from your account and sent to the scammer
A confirmation receipt will be downloaded
explanation: Entering your UPI PIN ALWAYS transfers money out of your bank. You never enter a PIN to receive funds.

question: You receive a video call from a man in police uniform claiming a parcel sent to Taiwan with drugs and passports has your Aadhaar number. He orders you to stay on video in 'Digital Arrest' and transfer 'bail security money'.
options: Transfer money quickly to prove your innocence to the officer
Stay in the room on video call until he gives clearance
Disconnect immediately. 'Digital Arrest' is a fake scam. Dial 1930.
explanation: There is no legal provision for 'Digital Arrest' in India. Police and court officials never conduct trials or bail demands over Skype/WhatsApp.

question: You receive an SMS: 'Dear Customer, your electricity bill is unpaid. Power supply will be disconnected at 9:30 PM tonight. Call electricity officer at 9876543210 immediately.'
options: Call the number in the SMS and follow their payment instructions
Do not call. Official electricity boards never use personal 10-digit mobile numbers for disconnections
Forward the SMS to all family members to warn them
explanation: Electricity boards (CSPDCL in Chhattisgarh) send notices via official alphanumeric sender IDs (e.g., CSPDCL), never personal 10-digit mobile numbers.

question: A customer care executive asks you to download 'AnyDesk' or 'RustDesk' on your mobile so he can fix your phone banking error.
options: Download it, as customer care needs to see your screen
Refuse and delete the app immediately. Screen sharing apps let scammers view your passwords and OTPs live
Share only the 9-digit code and keep the screen turned off
explanation: Screen sharing apps give complete live visibility and remote control of your phone, allowing scammers to steal OTPs as they arrive.

question: At an ATM counter in your town, a helpful stranger offers to help you insert your card when the machine is slow.
options: Hand over the card and tell him the PIN so he can withdraw faster
Politely decline, never let anyone see your card or keypad, and report faulty machines to the bank
Let him help if he is wearing a security uniform
explanation: Card swapping and PIN shoulder surfing are widespread. Never allow strangers near the machine while entering your PIN.

question: You scan a shop QR code that says 'Pay Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution'. But when scanned, the UPI ID shows 'rohitkumar982@okaxis'. What should you do?
options: Pay immediately because the shopkeeper said it works
Stop and do not pay. The name and handle indicate a personal account, not the official CSPDCL utility
Pay a test amount of ₹100 first
explanation: Always inspect the payee name and handle (pa). Utility billers and genuine businesses use verified business merchant handles.

question: You get a call from 'FedEx Courier' saying a customs duty of ₹1,450 must be paid via an SMS link to release an unexpected gift parcel from London.
options: Click the link and pay ₹1,450 to receive the surprise gift
Ignore or report. If you didn't order an international parcel, it is a custom duty parcel scam
Reply with your home address and Aadhaar card photo
explanation: Customs parcel scam lures victims with fake luxury gifts or illegal goods. Official customs never solicit payments to random UPI links.

question: An instant loan app offers ₹50,000 with zero documentation within 5 minutes, but requires access to your complete Contacts, Photos, and Media files.
options: Accept all permissions because the loan is fast
Never install predatory loan apps that demand contacts and photo permissions. They use them for blackmail
Upload only 10 contacts to test the app
explanation: Illegal lending apps harvest your contact book and private photos to harass and blackmail victims and family members.

question: If you or a neighbor accidentally sends money to a cyber fraudster, what is the single most critical immediate step?
options: Call the National Cyber Crime Helpline at 1930 within the 'Golden Hour' to freeze the funds
Wait 48 hours to see if the money returns automatically
Post on social media and wait for customer support reply
explanation: Calling 1930 within the first 1-2 hours allows cyber police to freeze the scammer's bank accounts before the money is withdrawn at an ATM.
